title: Heap Dump 与 HPROF 文件结构
key_conclusions: HPROF is a Java heap object-graph snapshot, not a profiler screenshot; its core evidence is records, heap sub-records, object ids, field references, arrays, classes, and GC roots.
A useful HPROF reading workflow starts from file structure, then reconstructs class schemas, object nodes, reference edges, roots, and finally Root-Owner-Bridge-Victim paths.
Android Studio, LeakCanary/Shark, and MAT can read the same dump but answer different questions: quick browsing, shortest retained path, and dominator/retained heap analysis.
HPROF does not prove fd, native heap, Graphics, or dma-buf lifetime, so resource and native cases still require meminfo, /proc fd, Perfetto, heapprofd, StrictMode, or CloseGuard evidence.
shallow_points: The article still explains representative HPROF structure rather than decoding a real target-app dump object by object.
It does not validate exact ART HPROF tags and dumpheap implementation against a checked-out Android branch.
It does not include exported Android Studio, Shark, and MAT screenshots or reports for the same HPROF.
It does not provide an automated script that diffs before/after class histograms or retained paths in CI.
